title: Shared mutable state needs common synchronization, not just some mutex
applies_when: A Go producer or recursive walker shares an error/stop variable across prefetch workers with different mutexes, or a background monitor updates a mutable policy such as disk-cache freeRatio while fullness/cleanup readers run outside the owner mutex.
lesson: Trace every read and write of the shared variable, not just whether each worker holds some lock. Different per-worker mutexes do not synchronize the traversal's write. A cache owner mutex also cannot protect a policy reader that runs outside it: use the same synchronization protocol for every runtime read/write and take one local snapshot per calculation. Keep traversal errors owner-local and use a shared atomic or common protocol for worker termination. Test the actual writer and real backend with matched before/after race runs. Keep reader results observable and confirm the regression detects the unchanged source; an initial baseline PASS is inconclusive, not qualification. A deferred stop covers error and successful early return; stopping future prefetch is not joining an already-running backend call.
avoid_when: A common lock or channel protocol already orders all relevant accesses, or the value is immutable. An atomic flag alone does not unblock stalled I/O or output, join goroutines, or make several related fields a consistent snapshot. Race-detector success covers only exercised schedules. Separate unrelated package-level races from the candidate by running the same command on unchanged source; passing leaf cases cannot override a failing package/process. A composition with an independent baseline fix is a separate source variant: record both exact changes and do not promote the combined result into standalone qualification.

evidence.note: Traversal writes captured err while workers read it under distinct listThread locks. Matched native Go race runs reproduce the conflicting accesses; those locks protect worker slots, not the shared traversal error.

Real in-memory nested listing tests cover all/deep/bounded output and initial/child/grandchild errors. Exact fixed source passes five focused race repeats and an object-package race run with disclosed TestDisk2 exclusion and environment skips. Proposed fix uses a walk-owned atomic stop; not full CI, cloud, joined-I/O or performance qualification.

The real ten-second cache lock checker raises freeRatio after its own temporary lock is removed. Matched native Linux Go runs report DATA RACE before the common-lock fix; six focused cases pass four race repeats after it, and the full chunk package passes without -race. Initial reader-only variants failed to detect the race and were not accepted as regression evidence. This is a proposed correctness fix, not full CI or a performance claim.
